title: 40 Taps a Day, Gone: How One Function Became My Conveyor | vitalii.no
description:
How chaining the whole publishing pipeline into a single Edge Function cut article latency from 15 minutes to 2, and manual taps to zero.

Even after moderation moved into Telegram, publishing was still a tap-fest. Every article needed four separate manual actions: trigger image generation, trigger the rewrite into three languages, publish to the website, and post to social. At 10 to 15 articles a day that came to 40 to 60 repetitive taps — none of which involved a decision. It was the same buttons in the same order, a factory line with no conveyor between the steps.

The auto-publish-news Supabase Edge Function, written in Deno, now orchestrates the entire chain. A new article triggers it and it calls each internal step in sequence: image generation, multilingual rewriting across English, Norwegian and Ukrainian, website publication, then social posting to Telegram, X, LinkedIn and Facebook. Nothing waits for a human between steps. The one thing that still stops the line is an exception: when the AI output genuinely needs judgement, it asks.

Publication latency fell 87 percent, from 15 minutes manual to 2 minutes automatic, and the taps went to zero. My role changed from processing every article to reviewing the ones that actually need a second opinion. Throughput is now bounded only by external API rate limits.
